name: Databricks

inputs.name: http_path
inputs.label: SQL warehouse HTTP path (Connection details, e.g. /sql/1.0/warehouses/abc123def456ghi7)

vs_properties.EXCLUDED_CAPABILITIES: JOIN, JOIN_CONDITION_EQUI, JOIN_TYPE_INNER, JOIN_TYPE_FULL_OUTER, JOIN_TYPE_LEFT_OUTER, JOIN_TYPE_RIGHT_OUTER

access: USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT on its tables, and CAN USE on the SQL warehouse
auth_hint: an expired or revoked token is refused the same way - create a new one in Databricks (Settings > Developer > Access tokens)

error_hint.text: Unity Catalog returned tables without their columns, which Databricks adapter 1.0.2 cannot read - the built-in samples catalog does this (measured); choose a catalog and schema your workspace owns

tips: Names arrive in upper case (CUSTOMER, C_NAME): no quotes needed.
STRING arrives as VARCHAR(2000000), BIGINT as DECIMAL(19,0).
notes: A personal access token only: it lives in the CONNECTION's password (USER 'token'). OAuth M2M is not offered - the adapter needs its client secret inside the JDBC URL (upstream issue 43).

Metadata comes from the Unity Catalog REST API through the Lua adapter, rows through IMPORT FROM JDBC. Upstream 1.0.2 turns certificate verification off for the REST calls (issue 4) because the database's LuaSec loads no CA file; the kit's suffix verifies the chain against the pinned Mozilla CA bundle and the host name against the certificate, in memory, before any request or token is sent - measured: Databricks verifies; an expired, self-signed, untrusted-root and wrong-host certificate are each refused.
The JDBC loader on Exasol Personal has no CA store of its own, so the loader's main class is the kit's exakit.loader.TrustStoreDriver (the language container's CA store), as for Snowflake.
The samples catalog cannot be read: its REST answer has no columns, and adapter 1.0.2 fails on that.

Joins are not pushed down (EXCLUDED_CAPABILITIES): adapter 1.0.2 renders a join of three tables as FROM `` and Databricks refuses it (measured). Each table is read with its own filters pushed down, and Exasol joins them - the same answers as Databricks, measured.
